nodes.title: Programming basics
nodes.why: Understanding basic programming constructs enables writing any backend code.
checkpoints: Variables store values of a specific data type and can be reassigned within their scope.
Control flow statements like if/else decide which block of code executes based on a condition.
Loops such as for and while repeat execution until a termination condition becomes false.

nodes.title: Web basics
nodes.why: Knowing how client‑server communication works underpins building HTTP services.
checkpoints: A client sends an HTTP request to a server, which returns a response containing status and data.
Stateless request-response model means each request is independent and does not rely on previous ones.
Web browsers interpret HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to render user interfaces.

nodes.title: Git workflow
nodes.why: Git workflow lets you manage code changes, collaborate via branches and pull requests.
checkpoints: A branch creates an independent line of development, allowing changes without affecting main.
Pull requests submit a branch’s changes for review before merging into the target branch.
Merging combines commit histories and can create a merge commit when histories diverge.

nodes.title: HTTP fundamentals
nodes.why: HTTP fundamentals are required to design correct REST endpoints and handle status codes.
checkpoints: GET requests retrieve resources without a request body, while POST sends data to create resources.
HTTP status code 404 indicates the server cannot find the requested resource.
Cache‑Control: max‑age directive tells browsers how long a response may be cached.

nodes.title: TypeScript
nodes.why: TypeScript provides type safety for the Node.js codebase used in the APIs.
checkpoints: TypeScript adds static type annotations that are checked at compile time before emitting JavaScript.
Interface definitions declare object shapes, enabling compile‑time verification of property existence.
The tsc compiler reports type errors such as assigning a string to a number variable.

nodes.title: Node.js runtime
nodes.why: Node.js runtime executes the TypeScript‑compiled JavaScript that powers the service.
checkpoints: Node.js uses an event‑driven, non‑blocking I/O model to handle many concurrent connections.
The require function loads CommonJS modules synchronously from the file system.
process.env provides access to environment variables at runtime.

nodes.title: REST API development
nodes.why: REST API development creates the endpoints that external clients will call.
nodes.quote: Build and test REST API endpoints
checkpoints: REST endpoints map HTTP methods to CRUD operations on resources.
Path parameters are extracted from the URL and passed to handler functions.
Returning a 201 status code signals that a new resource was successfully created.

nodes.title: Automated testing
nodes.why: Automated testing ensures each code change stays correct and catches regressions.
nodes.quote: Write automated tests with every change
checkpoints: Unit tests isolate a single function and assert expected output given specific inputs.
Test runners detect failing assertions and report the file and line of the failure.
Running tests in CI ensures code changes do not break existing functionality.

nodes.title: SQL basics
nodes.why: SQL basics allow writing queries that retrieve and aggregate data from PostgreSQL.
checkpoints: INNER JOIN returns rows with matching keys in both tables, excluding non‑matches.
GROUP BY aggregates rows sharing a column value, enabling SUM, COUNT, AVG calculations.
WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY, affecting which data is aggregated.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL schema
nodes.why: PostgreSQL schema design defines the tables storing invoices and payments.
checkpoints: Primary keys uniquely identify rows and are indexed automatically by PostgreSQL.
Foreign key constraints enforce referential integrity between related tables.
Migrations record incremental schema changes, allowing versioned upgrades and rollbacks.

nodes.title: Database indexing
nodes.why: Database indexing improves query performance when data volume grows.
nodes.quote: add indexes when queries slow down
checkpoints: Creating an index on a column speeds up SELECT queries using that column in WHERE clauses.
Indexes increase write latency because each INSERT must also update the index structures.
A composite index on (a, b) can be used for queries filtering by a and b together.

nodes.title: Database transactions
nodes.why: Transactions guarantee that invoices and their payments are saved atomically.
nodes.quote: Use transactions so that an invoice
checkpoints: A transaction groups multiple statements so either all commit or none do, ensuring atomicity.
If a statement fails, issuing ROLLBACK reverts all changes made in the transaction.
Isolation levels control visibility of intermediate transaction data to other concurrent sessions.

nodes.title: Auth and validation
nodes.why: Authentication and validation protect customer data and prevent malformed input.
checkpoints: Input validation rejects data that does not match expected type or format before processing.
Authentication verifies a user’s identity, often by checking tokens or session cookies.
Storing passwords with bcrypt hashes protects them from being recovered if the database leaks.

nodes.title: Log debugging
nodes.why: Log debugging helps locate production errors quickly.
nodes.quote: Review logs to trace production errors
checkpoints: Log entries typically include timestamps, severity levels, and contextual messages.
Filtering logs by error level isolates entries that indicate failures.
Stack traces in error logs pinpoint the function call sequence leading to an exception.
